unharnessed.meaning: Every fact survives, including the dateline, the 28 years, pneumonia, age 73, the Dempsey-Carpentier bout, the burial at Westerly, the three denominations with dates, Sara J. Timanus, six lectures a week in twenty-nine countries, "Rhetoric Made Racy" and the Twentieth Century Quarterly. The quotation "often proved a ride of lifelong shame and woe" is kept verbatim.
unharnessed.sense: Terms mostly fit: "barracking for prohibition", "his offsider", "sheer hard yakka", "the reform mob", "having a go at popular entertainment". "that sort of carry-on" adds a sneer the original's "similar movements" doesn't carry.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural Australian idiom used the way locals use it: "a real character around the congressional lobbies", "Never one to hold his tongue", "a red-hot go", "won't raise an eyebrow".
unharnessed.register: A full level-4 retelling, with swearing at dad level: "He wrote a bloody mountain of stuff on moral questions."
unharnessed.tone: Keeps the obituary's wry but respectful air, and the death and funeral are reported plainly ("died of pneumonia in a hospital here today"). A few lines tip a little cheeky: "that sort of carry-on", "his gob".
unharnessed.flow: Mostly smooth, with one tangled clause: "Dr. Crafts, who the blokes fighting the laws he pushed reckoned was a \"reform fanatic,\" was a real character".
unharnessed.variety: Wide range: "barracking", "carry-on", "of that ilk", "red-hot go", "offsider", "goings-on", "hard yakka", "gob", "ciggies", "never-say-die".
unharnessed.essence: Clearly the 1922 Crafts obituary, with the same structure, dateline, quoted title and closing catalogue of vices.

engine.meaning: Most text is untouched, but key details are changed: "Sunday baseball, dartses" replaces cigarettes with darts, the book title is altered to "Rhetoric Made Racy, ay.", and "a picturesque reckon" turns a figure into nonsense.
engine.sense: Several terms take the wrong sense: "picturesque reckon" (reckon is a verb), "dartses" for cigarettes, "his bloody attacks" (an intensifier where none belongs), "ay" inside a book title.
engine.authenticity: Stock bits bolted onto unchanged 1922 prose: "Jeez, after funeral services here tomorrow", "Well, he was 73 years old.", "Now, he was a prolific writer".
engine.register: Far lighter than level 4 in substance: whole paragraphs are verbatim ("Among reform leaders, few can have equaled Dr. Crafts in the amount of work done"), with jarring tokens dropped in.
engine.tone: The obituary's dignity is undercut by misplaced interjections at the death and funeral: "carked it at a hospital here today of pneumonia. Well, he was 73 years old." "Jeez, after funeral services".
engine.flow: Broken grammar and jarring joins: "a picturesque reckon in congressional lobbies", "Sunday baseball, dartses were a few of the objects", "Boston uni".
engine.variety: A few fillers ("Well,", "Now,", "Jeez", "ay") and "bloody"; little range.
engine.essence: Recognisably the original where untouched, but corrupted details and a mangled book title flatten what made it distinctive.

yarn.meaning: All the facts are present, but some liberties are taken: the quoted "often proved a ride of lifelong shame and woe" is paraphrased without quote marks ("often ended up a ride you'd be sorry and red-faced about for the rest of your days"), and "Fancy tryin' to call off the biggest fight of the year." adds a claim. Sara's "forceful" is softened to "threw her weight behind".
yarn.sense: Terms fit well: "barrackin' for prohibition", "stoush" for the bout, "the wowser who went after everything people did for a bit of fun", "good old puritan stock".
yarn.authenticity: Strong local idiom ("wowser", "stoush", "bugger-all rest", "by the bucketload"), but the relentless g-dropping ("startin'", "fightin'", "gettin'", "stoppin'", "goin'", "dancin'", "reformin'") tips toward stage-Australian.
yarn.register: Pub-yarn heavy, a shade past level 4, with stacked asides ("Listen to this.", "Didn't see that one comin'.", "Bloody tireless, he was."). Swearing stays at dad level.
yarn.tone: Turns a wry obituary into something closer to a roast: "Pneumonia got him.", "The fun police never had a harder-workin' officer." The death is reported more flippantly than the original allows.
yarn.flow: Lively and readable, with some choppy lines: "Crafts wanted 'em banned by law, the lot."
yarn.variety: Very varied: "carked it", "barrackin'", "stoush", "kept his trap shut", "old man", "yakka", "gob", "wowser", "fun police".
yarn.essence: Still recognisably the Crafts obituary, but the mocking frame pushes it toward a send-up of the man rather than a report of his death.

unharnessed.why: "carry-on" is mildly derisive; the original is neutral here.

unharnessed.original: charged by opponents of legislation he sponsored with being a "reform fanatic,"
unharnessed.why: A tangled relative clause that reads awkwardly aloud.

engine.why: Changes the list of vices: cigarettes become darts, in an ungrammatical plural.
Alters a quoted book title, the very detail the paragraph turns on.
"reckon" is a verb; the noun swap produces nonsense.

engine.quote: Jeez, after funeral services here tomorrow
engine.why: An exclamation in front of the funeral notice; tone-deaf in an obituary.
A filler interjection that makes the age sound like an afterthought.
The swear word lands as a gratuitous intensifier in neutral prose.
Abbreviates a proper name, which breaks it.

yarn.quote: which he said often ended up a ride you'd be sorry and red-faced about for the rest of your days
yarn.original: which he said "often proved a ride of lifelong shame and woe"
yarn.why: A direct quotation is paraphrased and stripped of its quote marks; in a news obituary the man's own words matter.

yarn.quote: Fancy tryin' to call off the biggest fight of the year.
yarn.why: Adds a claim (the biggest fight of the year) and a jeer.

yarn.original: died at a hospital here today of pneumonia
yarn.why: Flippant for the cause of death in an obituary.

yarn.quote: The fun police never had a harder-workin' officer.
yarn.why: An added punchline that tips the obituary into a roast.
Representative of near-constant g-dropping that reads as put-on.

summaries.unharnessed: A faithful, natural level-4 obituary that keeps every fact and quotation and a fitting wry tone. A couple of slightly cheeky word choices.
summaries.engine: Mostly untranslated, with interjections and word swaps that corrupt facts (darts for cigarettes, an altered book title) and jar the obituary's tone.
summaries.yarn: Vivid and very Australian, with excellent terms like "wowser" and "stoush", but over-egged, mocking in tone and loose with the quoted words.
